answer: The whisper multiplier is published, charged in pulse, and yarrow lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 2363 identities would post 3120 proofs and burn roughly 29 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
